label: first original token being read (t=0 or fed back at step L+1), in short sequences
predicate: ((recall_idx == 1) & (L == 3)) | ((recall_idx == 1) & (L == 4) & isin(in_tok, [tok("r"), tok("o"), tok("x"), tok("f"), tok("e"), tok("c")])) | ((t == 0) & isin(in_tok, [tok("r"), tok("o")]))
explanation: Fires only on steps where the input is the first original token. (1) Main mass (~80%): copy step L+1 (recall_idx==1), where orig(0) comes back in as input after <DEL>. Almost always active for L=3 (precision ~0.75, about half the total mass, top activations up to max). For L=4 it fires only on some first tokens (r, o, x, f, e, c most often) and with smaller magnitude. Essentially never active at recall_idx==1 for L>=5. (2) At t=0 when the first token is r or o: fires on almost every such sequence but very weakly (~0.06 of max for r, ~0.01 for o). This is ~20% of mass. Never active at the delimiter, at original steps t>=1, or at copy steps other than L+1 (apart from a handful at t=6). Magnitude mostly depends on sequence length (L=3 >> L=4) and on the identity of the first token.

issues: The headline numbers check out. recall_idx==1 & L==3 has dev precision 0.746 and 0.52 of the mass. recall_idx==1 & L==4 has 0.28 of the mass. t==0 with r has precision 1.0 and 0.17 mass; t==0 with o has precision 1.0 and 0.03 mass. recall_idx==1 & L>=5 has about 0.003 mass. Test scores reproduce (F1 0.854, mass recall 0.902).

The L=4 clause is systematically wrong. At recall_idx==1 with L=4, activation depends on all four original tokens, not just the first. Scanning orig(1), orig(2) and orig(3) shows strong selectivity at every position: v, k, d, w, 2, u, 3, t, p, q, b and s have precision 0.2-0.42, while 0, x, f, h, m and n are near 0.02-0.06. The test misses show this directly. Sequences starting with y, j, p, 0 or n, outside the first-token list, fire up to 0.18 of max, and x- and f-first sequences are false positives. The stated first-token list r/o/x/f/e/c reaches only 0.43 precision on this slice.
The 'apart from 45 dev activations at t=6' exception is mislabeled. All 45 are recall_idx==1 at L=5 (t=6 = L+1), so they belong to case 1, not to some other copy step.

The label and explanation overclaim. 'Fires only on steps where the input is the first original token' implies it fires whenever orig(0) is the input, but it is silent at t=0 for 28 of 30 first tokens and at step L+1 for L>=5. Also, the t=0 r/o clause does not depend on length, so 'in short sequences' covers only one of the two cases.
By step count, recall is dominated by the very weak t=0 r/o firings (about 61% of active steps but only 20% of the mass).
